html:
The global geopolitical landscape is dominated by escalating conflict between the United States and Iran, marked by renewed US strikes, a reinstated naval blockade of Iranian ports, and Iranian retaliatory attacks across the Gulf and on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. These actions have ignited concerns of a return to all-out war, driving up oil prices and exposing the fragility of a prior ceasefire deal.

US-Iran Conflict: The US has launched additional rounds of strikes on Iran and reimposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports, with President Trump initially threatening a 20% fee on Hormuz cargo before reversing that specific policy. Iran has declared the Strait of Hormuz closed, with its security committee chief stating Iranian MPs have presented a bill regarding the waterway. Iranian forces, including the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, have reportedly targeted US strategic assets and bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Qatar, destroyed a US MQ1 drone, and struck oil tankers in Hormuz, killing at least one Indian sailor. China has urged both nations to restore safe passage through the Strait, while Brazilian President Lula da Silva condemned Trump's proposed Hormuz toll as "piracy." The US has informed Congress of the resumption of fighting with Iran, with Senate Democrats blocking a defense bill over war funding.

Russia-Ukraine: The conflict continues with Russia hitting a civilian ship, killing three crew members, while Ukraine reports downing five Russian ballistic missiles and seeks faster weapons deliveries. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is moving to reshuffle his cabinet, and the Ukrainian parliament has accepted PM Svyrydenko's resignation. The Kremlin has stated that security guarantees for Ukraine are not possible without Russia's involvement.

US Domestic and Foreign Policy: Internally, Trump has paid E Jean Carroll $5m in damages over sexual abuse and defamation. Darline Graham, sister of the late Lindsey Graham, was sworn in to fill his Senate term. Federal immigration officials have been instructed to halt vehicle stops following three enforcement-related deaths in one week in Maine, Texas, and Florida, which have also strained Mexico-US relations. Top House Democrats are split over a proposed amendment to cut US military aid to Israel. Mahmoud Khalil has sued Trump officials and pro-Israel groups, alleging a conspiracy to target him for supporting Palestinian rights. Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey has called for international cooperation on AI threats, warning that the US and Trump administration cannot achieve their ambitions alone.

Global Economy: Oil prices have climbed 2% to a four-week high due to the intensifying tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. Diamond giant De Beers has halted work for two years at a flagship South African mine, citing plummeting demand. There is a global shortage of airplanes, which is contributing to increased flight prices. Separately, a survey suggests global productivity may be suffering from people watching the World Cup during work hours.

Middle East Regional Dynamics: Beyond the US-Iran clashes, Israeli strikes in north Gaza have killed seven, including a senior police officer, and separate Israeli drone strikes have killed Palestinians and a child in Gaza City and the southern Gaza Strip. The occupation government has allocated $434 million for 34 new West Bank settlements. In Yemen, the fragile peace is collapsing, with Saudi Arabia launching airstrikes on Sanaa airport, which Yemen considers an end to de-escalation, and Yemeni Armed Forces targeting Abha International Airport in response. Lebanon-Israel truce negotiations are stalled over withdrawal zones, though talks have resumed in Rome. The passing of Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the former Qatar Emir, has drawn condolences from world leaders.

Other Global Developments: In the United Kingdom, former politician and TV personality Ann Widdecombe was killed in a "targeted attack." The death toll from a music bar fire in Bangkok has risen to 30, with dozens remaining in hospital. A magnitude 6.2 earthquake struck off the southern Philippines, following a series of quakes in the Ring of Fire.
